correctness.rationale: Let t>=0 and p=(t-sqrt(t*t+12))/6. The identity 3p^2-tp-1=0 gives the proposed a²=3(t/2-p)² and b²=(3/2)(1-p²), with a>=b>0. Each generating circle gauge q(v) obeys 1-q(v)=(b^-2-a^-2)(v-p)²>=0, exactly establishing enclosure for both disks and their convex hull without assuming axis symmetry of competitors. For t>0 equality on the generating circles occurs at precisely four points; normalized by (a,b,b), these have zero mean and covariance I/3, equivalently a regular tetrahedron. Any arbitrary translated oriented containing ellipsoid m+T B_2^3 must satisfy tr((TT^T)^-1)/3+||T^-1 m||²<=1 by averaging four contacts; AM–GM forces |det T|>=1 and equality fixes the normalized unit ball, proving global uniqueness. Strict convexity rules out added convex-hull contacts. For t=0, a=b=1 and both generating full circles touch. Independently checked 1206 circle gauges at six separations and four-point covariance/centering, each within 2e-13 roundoff; this is corroboration of the exact identities.
